zones.label: notch
zones.summary: Notch and dot always agree — either one marks Pin 1.
facts: The semicircular notch is cut into the end of the package nearest pin 1.
The pressed dot sits in the corner beside pin 1 itself, as a second check.
If the plastic is worn and you can only find one of the two, that one is enough.
Position: 0 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q1 — Parallel output 1 — drives one LED of the bar graph.
Position: 15 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: VCC — Positive supply.
Position: 1 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q2 — Parallel output 2.
Position: 14 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q0 — Parallel output 0 — the first LED of the bar graph.
Position: 2 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q3 — Parallel output 3.
Position: 13 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: SER — Serial data in — the bit that gets shifted in on the next clock.
Position: 3 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q4 — Parallel output 4.
Position: 12 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: OE' — Output enable, active low. Take it high to blank all outputs without losing the stored bits.
Position: 4 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q5 — Parallel output 5.
Position: 11 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: RCLK — Latch clock. A pulse here copies the register onto the output pins.
Position: 5 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q6 — Parallel output 6.
Position: 10 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: SRCLK — Shift clock. Each rising edge shifts one bit further along the register.
Position: 6 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: Q7 — Parallel output 7 — the far end of the bar.
Position: 9 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: SRCLR' — Shift-register clear, active low. Pull it low to wipe the register to zeros.
Position: 7 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: GND — Ground, the negative supply connection.
Position: 8 pins counter-clockwise from the notch.
74HC595 function: QH' — Serial output — feeds the SER pin of the next chip when you daisy-chain.

zones.label: backwards?
zones.summary: Rotate the chip 180° and both markers move together — but every pin lands in the wrong column.
facts: Pin 1 (Q1) would sit where pin 16 (VCC) belongs, so the supply pins swap ends.
VCC into a Q output and ground into another is the fastest way to destroy the chip.
The notch and the dot always move together, so either one catches the mistake.

quiz.question: Which pin do you clock to shift one more bit along the register?
quiz.explanation: SRCLK on pin 11 is the shift clock.

quiz.question: Which pin blanks every output without erasing the stored bits?
quiz.explanation: OE' on pin 13 mutes the outputs; the register keeps its contents.

quiz.question: Which pin feeds the SER input of a second chip when daisy-chaining?
quiz.explanation: QH' on pin 9 is the serial output.

quiz.question: Which two markers on the package tell you where pin 1 is?
quiz.explanation: The notch and the pressed dot — they always agree.

quiz.question: Which pin is the positive supply?
quiz.explanation: VCC is pin 16, diagonally opposite pin 1's end of the count.
